title: STARLIGHT 2.0: Strategic Litigation for Rights in Europe | Applications Open
summary: Across Europe, democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights continue to face significant pressure. The EU Charter of Fundamental Rights provides an important legal framework for protecting these rights, but its potential as a tool for strategic litigation remains underused. STARLIGHT 2.0 – Strategic Litigation for Rights in Europe is now accepting applications from legal professionals who want to strengthen their ability to use the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights to pursue systemic change and improve rights protection across Europe. The programme brings together legal training, practical skills development, mentorship, legal clinics and networking opportunities to help participants turn strategic litigation into a tool for lasting impact. The programme is delivered by Democracy Reporting International, the Hertie School and the Hungarian Helsinki Committee , with support from the European Commission s CERV programme. About STARLIGHT 2.0 STARLIGHT 2.0 is designed for legal professionals who already have experience in litigation and want to develop stronger knowledge and practical strategies for using the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights in strategic cases. The programme focuses on how litigation can go beyond resolving individual cases and contribute to broader changes in law, policy, institutional practice and rights protection . Participants will learn from experienced academics, practitioners and litigators while working with peers from across EU Member States. The programme also includes legal clinics and mentorship to help participants apply what they learn to real-world cases. What the STARLIGHT 2.0 Programme Offers The programme combines several forms of professional learning and collaboration. Practical Legal and Skills Training Participants will take part in in-person training sessions designed to strengthen both their legal knowledge and practical professional skills. The programme s 2026–2027 cohort includes: In-person Charter training Skills training Online legal clinics Mentorship Peer learning Networking with other legal professionals The in-person Charter training is scheduled for 9–11 November 2026 , while the skills training is scheduled for 1–3 March 2027 . Expert Guidance Participants will learn from experienced academics, legal practitioners and strategic litigators with expertise in using the EU Charter and pursuing rights-based litigation. The programme is designed to connect participants with people who have practical experience in developing litigation strategies and using legal cases to achieve systemic change. Legal Clinics and Mentorship Participants will have opportunities to work through real-life cases and develop legal strategies with support from experts and mentors. The legal clinics are an important part of the programme because they allow participants to apply knowledge from the training to practical litigation challenges. European Network STARLIGHT 2.0 also provides participants with an opportunity to connect with legal professionals from across Europe. The programme aims to build a growing community of practitioners who can share knowledge, strategies and best practices while working to strengthen fundamental rights protection. The first cohort included lawyers from NGOs, National Human Rights Institutions and law firms across the EU. Two Thematic Streams Applicants can participate in one of two thematic areas. Democracy and Rule of Law This stream focuses on strategic litigation related to: Democracy Rule of law Fundamental rights Civic space Democratic institutions Systemic rights violations Participants explore how strategic litigation can influence law, policy and public debate. Asylum and Migration The second stream focuses on legal issues involving: Asylum Migration Fundamental rights Protection of migrants and refugees Strategic litigation Applicants should select the stream that most closely aligns with their professional interests and experience. Who Can Apply? The STARLIGHT 2.0 call is open to legal practitioners working in EU Member States . Eligible applicants include legal professionals working in: Law firms Civil society organisations Legal clinics National Human Rights Institutions Applicants should have at least two years of relevant professional experience . The programme is intended for experienced legal professionals who are interested in using strategic litigation to strengthen democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights. Eligibility Requirements Applicants should meet the following requirements: Be a legal practitioner working in an EU Member State . Work in a law firm, civil society organisation, legal clinic or National Human Rights Institution. Have at least two years of relevant professional experience . Have an interest in strategic litigation and fundamental rights. Be interested in using the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights in practical litigation. Be prepared to actively participate throughout the programme. The available information does not indicate that the programme is limited to lawyers working in a particular academic specialisation. Applicants should therefore demonstrate how their current legal work connects to the programme s thematic areas. Scholarships and Financial Support Selected participants will receive scholarships covering the training fees and accommodation in Berlin for the three-day in-person legal and skills workshops. However, travel costs are self-funded . This means participants will need to arrange and finance their own travel to and from Berlin, while the programme covers the specified training fees and accommodation. Programme Timeline The current STARLIGHT 2.0 cohort will run from: October 2026 to July 2027 Key in-person training dates include: Charter Training: 9–11 November 2026 Skills Training: 1–3 March 2027 The programme also includes online clinics, mentorship and additional engagement during the programme period. Why Strategic Litigation Matters Strategic litigation can be used to pursue changes that extend beyond the outcome of an individual legal case. A carefully selected case can potentially influence: Legal interpretation Government policy Institutional practice Protection of fundamental rights Public debate Implementation of court decisions STARLIGHT 2.0 is designed to help legal professionals understand how to identify cases with broader potential and develop litigation strategies that can contribute to systemic change. ( DevelopmentAid ) What Participants Can Gain Through the programme, participants can develop: Stronger Knowledge of the EU Charter Gain a deeper understanding of how the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights can be used in strategic litigation. Practical Litigation Skills Learn approaches for developing and pursuing cases with potential for broader impact. Expert Mentorship Receive guidance from experienced legal practitioners and academics. Case-Based Learning Apply programme knowledge to real-life cases through legal clinics. Professional Network Connect with other legal professionals working on fundamental rights and strategic litigation across Europe. Skills for Systemic Impact Learn how litigation can contribute to changes beyond individual cases, including changes to law, policy and public debate. Who Is This Opportunity Best Suited For? STARLIGHT 2.0 may be particularly relevant to legal professionals working on: Human rights Fundamental rights Democracy Rule of law Civic space Asylum Migration Strategic litigation Legal advocacy Rights protection It is especially relevant to practitioners who want to strengthen their ability to use the EU Charter as part of their litigation strategy. Application Deadline The application deadline for the current cohort is: 20 September 2026 Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and carefully review all programme requirements before applying. How to Apply Interested legal professionals should apply through the official STARLIGHT 2.0 application process. The programme information and application details are available through the official programme organisers. Consider Your Travel Arrangements Although training fees and accommodation in Berlin are covered through scholarships, travel is self-funded . Applicants should plan accordingly. Conclusion STARLIGHT 2.0 – Strategic Litigation for Rights in Europe provides legal professionals across EU Member States with an opportunity to strengthen their ability to use the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights as a tool for strategic litigation and systemic rights protection. The programme combines legal training, practical skills development, online legal clinics, mentorship and professional networking. Participants can choose between the Democracy Rule of Law and Asylum Migration streams while working with experienced practitioners and peers from across Europe. title: CPJ Recruitment 2026: Apply for Remote Press Freedom Positions in Europe and Central Asia
summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists is accepting applications for two remote positions within its Europe and Central Asia programme. These opportunities are intended for experienced professionals with backgrounds in journalism, media freedom, human rights, research, advocacy, humanitarian assistance and regional policy. As verified on September 1, 2026, the official CPJ employment page lists the following vacancies: Program Coordinator, Eastern Europe/Central Asia Researcher, Western and Northern Europe Both positions are classified as remote, Europe-based roles and will be filled through an Employer of Record arrangement. Candidates must be based in the relevant Europe and Central Asia region and possess independent authorization to work from their proposed location. The closing date for both positions is September 10, 2026. CPJ has not specified a precise closing time or time zone, so interested candidates should apply well before the deadline. Overview of the Available CPJ Positions Position Programme Work Arrangement Experience UK Salary Reference Deadline Program Coordinator, Eastern Europe/Central Asia Europe and Central Asia Fully remote, Europe-based At least seven years £72,250–£84,000 September 10, 2026 Researcher, Western and Northern Europe Europe and Central Asia Fully remote, Europe-based At least five years £45,700–£51,500 September 10, 2026 The salary figures above apply as reference ranges for candidates hired in the United Kingdom. Compensation for candidates working from other eligible locations will be determined according to their experience, skills, local market conditions and cost of living. About the Committee to Protect Journalists Founded in 1981, the Committee to Protect Journalists, commonly known as CPJ, is an independent nonprofit organisation that works to defend journalists and advance press freedom around the world. CPJ monitors, verifies and reports attacks against journalists and media workers. Its work includes documenting press freedom violations, advocating for imprisoned or threatened journalists, supporting journalists facing emergencies and encouraging legal and policy reforms that protect freedom of expression. Over more than four decades, CPJ has contributed to efforts that have: Secured the early release of imprisoned journalists. Helped advance accountability for the murders of journalists. Supported legal reforms in countries where freedom of expression has deteriorated. Raised international awareness of attacks on journalists. Produced widely cited research, databases and reports concerning press freedom. Provided assistance to journalists facing physical, digital, legal and psychological threats. Although CPJ is headquartered in New York City, its staff members and contributors work across different regions. The organisation seeks employees who can collaborate effectively across countries, cultures and time zones. Position One: Program Coordinator, Eastern Europe/Central Asia Position Overview The Program Coordinator will lead CPJ’s research, documentation, advocacy and journalist-support activities relating to Eastern Europe and Central Asia. The position sits within CPJ’s Europe and Central Asia programme and reports to the Regional Director for Europe and Central Asia. It is classified within CPJ’s Management II job band. CPJ is looking for an experienced professional with extensive knowledge of press freedom conditions in Russia and Eastern Europe and a strong understanding of the wider regional political, human rights and media environment. The selected candidate will coordinate regional contributors, oversee press freedom monitoring, support journalists facing danger and represent CPJ before media organisations, government representatives, civil society partners and other stakeholders. This is a leadership position requiring both strategic oversight and hands-on involvement in research, reporting, advocacy, crisis response and team management. Team Coordination and Leadership Responsibilities The Program Coordinator will provide day-to-day leadership and supervision to staff members and regional contributors. Responsibilities will include: Establishing clear expectations for staff and contributors. Assigning and delegating work according to programme priorities. Monitoring the quality, accuracy and timeliness of regional work. Coaching and developing team members. Addressing performance or conduct concerns when necessary. Promoting an inclusive, accountable and high-performing team culture. Supporting the recruitment and onboarding of employees and contributors. Managing researchers, correspondents, contractors and other regional contributors. Ensuring that regional work aligns with CPJ’s organisational strategy and standards. Deputising for senior regional leadership when required. Supporting the implementation of wider regional strategies and priorities. Providing crisis-management leadership during urgent or high-risk press freedom situations. Applicants should demonstrate experience supervising people, coordinating distributed teams and maintaining professional standards under pressure. Press Freedom Monitoring, Research and Data Responsibilities A major part of the position involves ensuring that CPJ receives reliable, current and well-documented information concerning attacks on journalists. The Program Coordinator will be expected to: Monitor press freedom developments across Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Document and report attacks, threats and restrictions affecting journalists. Maintain oversight of press freedom case-tracking and advocacy pipelines. Ensure that CPJ’s records concerning imprisoned, missing, killed or targeted journalists remain accurate and current. Identify emerging threats and trends affecting journalists and media organisations. Propose, commission, supervise and conduct regional research. Produce daily reporting, longer analytical reports and multimedia content. Prepare timely news alerts, statements, videos and expert analysis. Develop factual social media material in coordination with CPJ’s communications and social media teams. Contribute to annual regional assessments, planning documents and strategic reviews. The successful candidate must be capable of moving between immediate breaking-news responses and deeper, long-term research projects. Advocacy Responsibilities The Program Coordinator will play a leading role in developing and implementing advocacy strategies intended to improve protections for journalists. Duties will include: Designing regional and country-level press freedom advocacy strategies. Advocating for the release of journalists who have been imprisoned because of their work. Supporting efforts to end impunity in cases involving the killing of journalists. Producing advocacy briefings and other supporting materials. Overseeing the preparation of advocacy content. Developing new projects in response to emerging political and media developments. Presenting CPJ’s research to media outlets, policymakers and other stakeholders. Using evidence and documented cases to influence public and policy discussions. Applicants should understand how research, public communication, stakeholder engagement and policy advocacy can be combined to produce practical pressure for change. Representation and External Engagement The position requires the selected candidate to represent CPJ publicly and maintain a strong network of regional contacts. The Program Coordinator will: Act as a CPJ spokesperson when required. Engage with media outlets, governments, civil society groups and partner organisations. Develop and maintain relationships with policymakers and journalists. Strengthen CPJ’s network of regional media contacts. Establish relationships with human rights defenders and other relevant stakeholders. Develop collaborations, joint initiatives and coalition-based activities. Represent CPJ at national and regional meetings, forums and events. Travel within the region when required. Strong professional judgment will be essential because the position may involve communication about politically sensitive cases and engagement with journalists experiencing serious threats. Journalist Assistance and Safety Responsibilities The Program Coordinator will also support journalists who are experiencing threats, trauma or emergency situations. Responsibilities include: Developing journalist-assistance and advocacy plans. Reviewing requests for assistance from journalists. Assessing urgent cases and identifying appropriate responses. Providing first-responder support and feedback. Coordinating assistance with CPJ’s Journalist Assistance team. Preparing case-related documentation and reports. Working with the Emergencies team to monitor dangerous situations. Responding to new threats affecting journalists. Supporting the delivery of timely and appropriate assistance. Experience supporting people affected by trauma, persecution or emergency conditions is particularly valuable for this role. Internal Coordination and Reporting The Program Coordinator will work with CPJ teams responsible for advocacy, research and journalist assistance to ensure that regional activities contribute to the organisation’s wider objectives. The selected candidate will prepare activity reports, assessments and internal updates and may be assigned other responsibilities consistent with CPJ’s research and advocacy mandate. Required Qualifications for the Program Coordinator Applicants must possess the following qualifications and competencies: A bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience. At least seven years of experience in media or advocacy work connected to regional press freedom issues. Extensive knowledge of Russia, Eastern Europe and the wider Europe and Central Asia region. A deep understanding of the regional geopolitical environment. Demonstrated ability to analyse political, policy and freedom-of-expression issues. The ability to connect political developments with their consequences for journalists and press freedom. Strong research, analysis and reporting skills. Experience writing concise and high-quality reports. The ability to interpret, assess and accurately summarise reports and data. Fluency in spoken and written English. Fluency in spoken and written Russian. Working proficiency in other relevant regional languages. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Strong interpersonal, negotiation and conflict-resolution skills. Excellent organisational abilities and close attention to detail. Strong time-management skills and a record of meeting deadlines. Effective analytical and problem-solving abilities. The capacity to work with integrity, professionalism and confidentiality. Experience leading teams and working with senior managers. Willingness and ability to travel occasionally within the region. Proficiency in Google Workspace applications. Because the role includes emergency response and politically sensitive work, candidates must be able to make careful decisions, protect confidential information and remain effective in high-pressure situations. Preferred Qualifications for the Program Coordinator CPJ considers the following qualifications desirable: Knowledge of additional regional languages. An established network of professional contacts across the region. Expertise concerning online or digital harms, including surveillance. Experience contributing to policy development. Multimedia or data-journalism experience. Experience supporting journalists or other individuals affected by trauma. Experience managing journalist-assistance cases. Applicants who meet all essential requirements should not necessarily exclude themselves merely because they do not possess every preferred qualification. Work Location and Schedule The Program Coordinator position is: Fully remote. Located in Europe. Intended for a candidate based in the Europe and Central Asia region. Filled through an Employer of Record. Subject to occasional regional travel. Required to attend meetings conducted on United States Eastern Time when necessary. Remote status does not mean that applications are automatically accepted from every country. The application form expressly asks applicants to state where they are currently based, where they intend to work and whether they possess independent work authorization in that location. The vacancy does not state that CPJ will sponsor a visa, work permit or relocation. Program Coordinator Salary Compensation will depend on the selected candidate’s: Professional experience. Relevant skills. Country of employment. Local labour-market conditions. Cost of living. For a candidate hired in the United Kingdom, CPJ provides an expected annual salary reference of: £72,250 to £84,000 Candidates based in another eligible country should not assume that the UK salary range will apply. CPJ will determine location-specific compensation under the applicable Employer of Record arrangement. Position Two: Researcher, Western and Northern Europe Position Overview CPJ is also recruiting a Researcher focusing on Western and Northern Europe. The position is part of the Europe and Central Asia programme and reports to the Program Coordinator for Europe and Central Asia. The position is classified within the Researchers and Associates I job band and identified as a mid-level role. The Researcher will monitor, investigate, verify and document attacks on the press and other developments affecting media freedom. The position also involves preparing research and advocacy materials, supporting regional strategy, representing CPJ when required and assisting journalists facing threats or emergencies. The successful candidate must have substantial knowledge of media, press freedom and human rights issues in Europe and Central Asia, with particular strength in Western and Northern Europe. Monitoring, Data Collection and Documentation Responsibilities The Researcher will be responsible for tracking press freedom developments and ensuring that CPJ’s reporting is supported by verified evidence. Responsibilities include: Monitoring press freedom developments across Europe and Central Asia. Focusing particularly on Western and Northern Europe. Investigating and documenting arrests of journalists. Monitoring censorship and restrictions on media organisations. Recording physical attacks and threats against journalists. Examining legal harassment directed at journalists and media outlets. Monitoring transnational repression affecting journalists. Documenting other threats to press freedom. Maintaining current information in CPJ’s databases. Updating records concerning imprisoned, missing, killed or targeted journalists. Monitoring breaking news and emerging developments. Alerting the Program Coordinator promptly when an urgent issue arises. Developing and maintaining databases of media, government and civil-society contacts. Candidates must be able to verify information carefully and distinguish credible evidence from incomplete, misleading or politically motivated claims. Research and Writing Responsibilities The Researcher will produce content for CPJ’s reporting, advocacy and public communications. The selected candidate will: Initiate and write reports concerning regional press freedom. Produce advocacy documents and background materials. Write timely news alerts and public statements. Prepare expert analysis concerning regional developments. Conduct original research on press freedom issues. Prepare research notes in accordance with CPJ standards. Write factual and engaging social media content. Coordinate public-facing material with CPJ’s social media team. Contribute to longer-term research and reporting initiatives. Excellent English writing and reporting skills are essential. Applicants must be able to produce accurate material quickly without sacrificing verification or journalistic standards. Advocacy Responsibilities The Researcher will support and participate in CPJ’s regional advocacy activities. Responsibilities will include: Representing CPJ at relevant conferences and meetings. Participating in meetings with government authorities. Engaging with journalists, partner organisations and policymakers. Helping develop advocacy strategies for Europe and Central Asia. Implementing advocacy activities in coordination with the Program Coordinator and Regional Director. Participating in online and in-person meetings that advance CPJ’s press freedom objectives. The role requires candidates who can explain complex political and media issues clearly to different audiences. Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination The Researcher will build relationships with people and organisations relevant to CPJ’s work. This includes: Developing relationships with journalists. Maintaining contacts with human rights organisations. Engaging with civil society and other regional stakeholders. Coordinating joint activities that advance CPJ’s objectives. Collaborating with CPJ’s advocacy, research and assistance teams. Presenting CPJ research to media outlets and other stakeholders. Helping influence coverage of important press freedom developments. A strong regional network is preferred, although it is not listed as an absolute requirement. Journalist Assistance Responsibilities The Researcher will support CPJ’s work with journalists who require assistance. Duties include: Researching and verifying journalist-assistance requests. Preparing assistance documentation in accordance with CPJ’s internal framework. Coordinating with the Emergencies team. Communicating and coordinating with journalists receiving support. Helping ensure that assistance decisions are based on accurate and properly documented information. Experience with trauma-related cases or journalist-assistance work is considered an advantage. Translation and Additional Support The Researcher may be asked to translate interviews, documents and other materials between English and relevant regional languages. The selected candidate may also perform other responsibilities that fall within CPJ’s research and advocacy mandate. Required Qualifications for the Researcher Applicants must possess: At least five years of experience researching, reporting and publishing on global human rights and political issues; or equivalent experience in advocacy and humanitarian assistance. Strong knowledge of Europe and Central Asia. A solid understanding of regional media and human rights issues. Excellent English writing and reporting skills. Proficiency in at least one additional language relevant to the position. Strong interpersonal and organisational skills. Effective time-management abilities. The capacity to act with integrity, professionalism and confidentiality. Significant experience engaging governments and policymakers. Knowledge of social media tools and the ability to use them effectively. Proficiency in Google Workspace, including Gmail, Calendar, Docs, Sheets and Drive. The ability to work independently and collaboratively. The ability to perform effectively in a fast-paced working environment. A clear commitment to press freedom. The capacity to work with minimal supervision. Unlike the Program Coordinator vacancy, the Researcher listing does not prescribe a bachelor’s degree as a mandatory qualification. Relevant professional experience, subject knowledge and language ability are central requirements. Preferred Qualifications for the Researcher The following experience and capabilities are desirable: Knowledge of additional regional languages. Strong professional networks within the region. Expertise relating to digital or online harms. Policy-development experience. Multimedia journalism experience. Data-journalism skills. Experience supporting trauma-related cases. Previous involvement in journalist-assistance work. Researcher Work Location and Schedule The Researcher position is: Fully remote. Located in Europe. Intended for a candidate based in the Europe or Central Asia region. Filled through an Employer of Record. Required to attend meetings conducted on United States Eastern Time when necessary. Applicants must possess independent authorization to work in the city and country from which they intend to perform the role. The announcement does not promise work-visa sponsorship or relocation assistance. Researcher Salary Compensation will depend on experience, skills and location. For candidates hired in the United Kingdom, the expected annual salary range is: £45,700 to £51,500 Candidates hired in other eligible locations may receive a different salary based on local market conditions and cost-of-living differences. Candidates should first visit the official CPJ employment page and select the appropriate position. Direct official vacancy pages are available below: Program Coordinator, Eastern Europe/Central Asia Researcher, Western and Northern Europe Applicants should ensure that they select the correct vacancy because the two application forms contain different experience and document requirements. Application Requirements for the Program Coordinator The Program Coordinator application form requests: First and last name. Email address. Telephone number. Full residential address. City, state or equivalent area, postal code and country. A cover letter. A résumé or curriculum vitae. Proposed availability date. Website, blog or portfolio link, where applicable. LinkedIn profile, where applicable. Highest educational qualification. Source of referral. Current city and country of residence. City and country from which the applicant intends to work. Confirmation that the applicant has independent work authorization. An explanation of why the applicant wants to work for CPJ. A list of languages and the applicant’s proficiency in speaking, reading or writing each language. Confirmation of the applicant’s years of media or advocacy experience relating to press freedom. Optional Demographic Questions Both application forms contain optional questions concerning: Gender Ethnicity Disability Veteran status CPJ expressly states that answers to these questions are optional and will not be used as selection criteria. Important Application Clarifications Applicants should understand the following points before applying: The positions are remote but not unrestricted global roles. Candidates must be based in the relevant Europe and Central Asia region. Independent work authorization is required. Applicants must already be legally authorized to work in their proposed location. Visa sponsorship is not promised. Neither announcement states that CPJ will arrange a work visa or sponsor relocation. The UK salary ranges are reference figures. Candidates must be available for meetings held according to United States Eastern Time when required. The Program Coordinator requires fluent English and Russian. Excellent English and proficiency in at least one other language relevant to Western and Northern Europe are required. No detailed employee-benefits package is included in the listings. CPJ states that reasonable accommodations may be made to enable candidates with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Commitment to journalist safety and freedom of expression. Evidence of meeting deadlines in fast-moving situations. Candidates for the Program Coordinator position should emphasise leadership, supervision, crisis management, regional advocacy and Russian-language proficiency. Candidates for the Researcher position should emphasise verification, research, reporting, writing, language ability and knowledge of Western and Northern European press freedom issues. Applicants should also check that all uploaded files are readable and appropriately named. A tailored résumé and concise cover letter should explain how the candidate’s specific experience matches CPJ’s regional requirements. Equal Employment Opportunity CPJ states that it provides equal employment opportunities and prohibits discrimination or harassment based on: Race Colour Religion Sex Pregnancy Gender identity Sexual orientation Parental status National origin Age Disability Genetic information or family medical history Political affiliation Military service Other non-merit-based considerations Candidates are assessed according to their experience, competencies, regional knowledge, language ability, work authorization and suitability for the position. The Program Coordinator position is suited to a senior professional with at least seven years of relevant experience, strong leadership credentials, extensive regional knowledge and fluency in English and Russian. The Researcher position is intended for a mid-level professional with at least five years of relevant research, reporting, advocacy or humanitarian-assistance experience. title: UN Junior Professional Officer Programme 2026 | Three Positions Open
summary: The United Nations Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme 2026 is inviting applications from qualified young professionals for three JPO positions within the United Nations system. The current call features opportunities in Political Affairs in New York, Humanitarian Affairs in East Jerusalem, and UN System Coordination in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire . All three positions are funded by Belgium and have an initial one-year contract that may be renewed annually for a maximum period of three years. ( FPS Foreign Affairs ) The application deadline for all three positions is 18 September 2026 at 6:00 PM Eastern Time (New York) . ( FPS Foreign Affairs ) About the UN Junior Professional Officer Programme The Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme is a United Nations training initiative that provides young professionals with an opportunity to gain practical experience within UN organisations, funds, programmes, and offices involved in development and international cooperation. Through the programme, JPOs work within UN organisations connected to Belgium s international development cooperation policy. Depending on the position, assignments can be based in partner countries, regional offices, or headquarters. JPOs receive professional training and guidance from senior staff members and can become involved in areas including: Programme design Programme formulation Programme implementation Programme monitoring Programme evaluation Policy and coordination work Development and humanitarian activities The Belgian government currently funds JPO positions across 18 UN organisations, funds, programmes and offices , including UNDP, UNICEF, WFP, FAO, UNHCR, WHO, UNFPA, UN Women, UNEP, IOM, OHCHR and OCHA. Current JPO Opportunities Three positions are currently available under the 2026 Belgian JPO call. 1. JPO in Political Affairs – Support to UN Reform Organisation: United Nations Executive Office of the Secretary-General (EOSG), Office of the Under-Secretary-General for Policy, UN80 Secretariat Location: New York, USA Field: Political Affairs / UN Reform The position focuses on supporting work related to UN reform and political affairs within the UN80 Secretariat. Eligibility and Qualifications Applicants must: Hold Belgian citizenship . Be 32 years old or younger as of 31 December 2026. Be born on or after 1 January 1994 . Hold an advanced university degree, such as a master s degree or equivalent , in: Political Science International Relations International Humanitarian Law Human Rights Social Sciences or another related field. Have at least two years of relevant professional experience in political affairs, development and/or humanitarian work. Have relevant experience with governments, international organisations, NGOs or research institutes. Experience with the UN or other international or non-governmental organisations is considered an advantage. Strong research, analytical and writing skills, as well as organisational abilities, are also preferred. Language Requirements Fluent English is required. Knowledge of French is desirable, while knowledge of another official UN language is an advantage. Important Experience Requirement Applicants work experience within the UN organisation to which they are applying must not exceed one year , including internships, UN Volunteers and consultancies. Relevant internships and volunteering may be counted at 50%. 2. JPO in Humanitarian Affairs Organisation: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), Operations and Advocacy Division, Country Office in the occupied Palestinian territory (oPt) Location: East Jerusalem Field: Humanitarian Affairs This position is focused on humanitarian affairs and supports work related to humanitarian operations and advocacy. Eligibility and Qualifications Applicants must: Hold Belgian citizenship . Be 32 years old or younger as of 31 December 2026. Be born on or after 1 January 1994 . Hold an advanced university degree, such as a Master s degree , in: Political or Social Science International Relations Public Administration Law Economics Engineering Earth Sciences A related field. Have at least two years of relevant professional experience in humanitarian affairs, emergency preparedness, crisis or emergency relief management, rehabilitation, development, or related areas. Have experience in information analysis . Experience working with international humanitarian agencies, the UN system, or in the occupied Palestinian territory context is considered desirable. Language Requirements Fluency in English is required. Knowledge of Arabic is an advantage. As with the other positions, work experience within the UN organisation to which the candidate is applying must not exceed one year, including internships, UNV and consultancies. 3. JPO in Coordination – UN System Coordination Organisation: United Nations Resident Coordinator System (RCS), Resident Coordinator Office (RCO) Location: Abidjan, Côte d Ivoire Field: UN System Coordination This position focuses on coordination within the UN Resident Coordinator System and provides an opportunity to contribute to cooperation and coordination across the UN system. Eligibility and Qualifications Applicants must: Hold Belgian citizenship . Be 32 years old or younger as of 31 December 2026. Be born on or after 1 January 1994 . Hold a Master s degree or equivalent advanced degree in: Development International Relations Political Science Economics Management A related field. Have at least two years of professional experience in a relevant field . Language Requirements Fluency in French is required. Knowledge of other official UN languages, particularly English, is an advantage. General Eligibility Requirements Although the three positions have different academic and professional requirements, the current Belgian-funded JPO call has several common eligibility conditions. Belgian Citizenship The current vacancies explicitly state that candidates must hold Belgian citizenship . The Belgian Foreign Affairs website explains that most Belgian-funded JPO positions are reserved for Belgian nationals. A limited number of positions may be reserved for candidates from Belgium s partner countries, but this must be specifically indicated in the relevant vacancy announcement. ( FPS Foreign Affairs ) Therefore, applicants should not assume that every Belgian-funded JPO position is open to applicants from all countries. Age Requirement Candidates must be 32 years old or younger on 31 December 2026 . For the current positions, this means candidates must have been born on or after 1 January 1994 . Master s Degree A master s degree or equivalent advanced university degree is required, although the acceptable field differs according to the position. Professional Experience The current positions generally require a minimum of two years of relevant professional experience . Applicants should make sure that their experience is directly related to the responsibilities and subject area of the position for which they are applying. UN Experience Limitation For the current positions, professional experience within the specific UN organisation to which the applicant is applying should not exceed one year , including internships, UN Volunteers and consultancies. Relevant internships and volunteering may be counted at 50%. title: Youth Connect: Youth Champions for Environment and Peace 2026 | Apply by 20 September
summary: The Youth Connect: Youth Champions for Environment and Peace 2026 programme is inviting young people living in Cyprus to join an intercommunal youth initiative focused on environmental peacebuilding, sustainability, dialogue, and joint environmental action . Organised through the regional Youth Connect programme , in collaboration with UNFICYP , the programme will bring together young people from different communities in Cyprus for an immersive workshop at the Ledra Palace Hotel in Nicosia . Participants will develop the knowledge, confidence, and practical skills needed to work together on environmental challenges and develop action plans that can contribute to a more peaceful, sustainable, cohesive, and resilient Cyprus. The programme will take place on 3, 4, 10 and 11 October 2026 , with environmental actions expected to be implemented by February 2027 . Participation is free . About the Youth Champions for Environment and Peace Programme The Youth Champions for Environment and Peace programme focuses on the connection between environmental challenges and peacebuilding . Climate change, environmental degradation, resource pressures, insecurity, and inequality can affect communities in different ways. The programme seeks to empower young people to work across community divisions and develop practical responses to shared environmental concerns. Through workshops, group activities, discussions, mentoring, and action planning, participants will have the opportunity to learn from environmental and peace activists while collaborating with other young people from across Cyprus. The programme is designed to strengthen: Environmental awareness Peacebuilding skills Social cohesion Intercommunal trust Inclusive leadership Critical thinking Confidence Adaptability Environmental cooperation Sustainable development Participants will also become part of a wider network of Youth Champions for Environment and Peace , connecting them with local and international organisations, activists, and other young people working on related issues. What the Programme Will Involve The programme consists of an immersive in-person workshop followed by the development and implementation of environmental actions. 1. Immersive Workshop The workshop will take place on: 3, 4, 10 and 11 October 2026 at the: Ledra Palace Hotel, Nicosia The sessions will focus on joint learning and collaboration between participants from different communities. The workshop will include: Interactive learning sessions Group work Discussions with environmental activists Discussions with peacebuilding activists Team-building activities Development of environmental action ideas Opportunities to build relationships with other participants During the group work, participants will form teams and work together to develop environmental actions with support from the programme team. Participation on all four workshop days is mandatory. Environmental Action Projects Following the workshop, participants will be expected to finalise their environmental action plans and submit a simple proposal for funding. Each team will receive a small grant to implement its action, with support from a mentor and experts. The environmental actions must be implemented by: February 2027 The actions should reach people across the divide and may take place throughout Cyprus. This component gives participants an opportunity to move beyond discussions and turn their ideas into practical environmental initiatives. Who Can Apply? The programme is specifically seeking dynamic and passionate young people who are living in Cyprus and are interested in contributing to a peaceful and sustainable future. Applicants must: Be 18–30 years old . Be from any community and be living in Cyprus. Have an interest in the environment and peacebuilding. Be interested in becoming active in environmental and peacebuilding issues. Have an interest in contributing to a peaceful and sustainable future in Cyprus. Be committed and motivated to participate actively throughout the entire workshop. Be willing to work as part of a team to develop and implement an environmental action. Have a very good knowledge of English . Be willing to develop interpersonal relationships with participants from all communities living in Cyprus. Be interested in working together with others toward a common cause. Previous Experience Is Not Required Applicants do not need previous experience in environmental peacebuilding or environmental activism. The programme is designed to provide participants with the knowledge, tools, and support required to develop their own environmental actions. However, applicants should demonstrate genuine interest in environmental issues, peacebuilding, cooperation, and creating a sustainable future for Cyprus. Previous Youth Champions Participants The call is specifically open to people who did not benefit from previous UN Youth Champions programmes . Applicants who have previously participated in a UN Youth Champions programme should therefore carefully consider this requirement before applying. Gender and Community Representation The organisers aim to promote gender diversity and equal representation among young people from all communities in Cyprus . This reflects the programme s broader objective of encouraging dialogue, cooperation, trust-building, and joint action among young people from different communities. Accommodation Accommodation in Nicosia may be available on 3 and 10 October , depending on demand. However, accommodation availability is limited and subject to confirmation . Applicants should therefore not assume that accommodation will automatically be provided and should consider this when planning their participation. Important Access Requirement All programme activities will take place at the Ledra Palace Hotel , which is located in the UN buffer zone in Nicosia. Participation is therefore dependent on the applicant s ability to enter the UN buffer zone in Nicosia . The organisers note that the respective sides have authority over entry from the crossing points, rather than the UN. Applicants should ensure that they have the required documentation to enter the buffer zone before applying. Certificate of Participation Participants who attend all four days of the workshop and actively contribute to the environmental actions will receive a certificate of participation . Benefits of Participating The Youth Champions for Environment and Peace programme provides participants with an opportunity to gain practical experience while contributing to environmental and peacebuilding efforts in Cyprus. Participants can: Develop Environmental Peacebuilding Skills Learn how environmental challenges can be addressed through cooperation, dialogue, and peacebuilding. Work Across Communities Build relationships and collaborate with young people from different communities in Cyprus. Develop an Environmental Action Work in a team to design an environmental initiative addressing a common concern. Receive Mentorship Receive support from mentors and experts while developing and implementing an environmental action. Access Small-Grant Support Teams will receive a small grant to support implementation of their environmental action following the workshop. Strengthen Leadership Skills Develop confidence, adaptability, critical thinking, interpersonal skills, and inclusive leadership abilities. Expand Your Network Connect with local and international organisations, activists, experts, trainers, and members of the Youth Champions network. Programme Schedule Activity Date Workshop Day 1 3 October 2026 Workshop Day 2 4 October 2026 Workshop Day 3 10 October 2026 Workshop Day 4 11 October 2026 Environmental Actions By February 2027 Location: Ledra Palace Hotel, Nicosia, Cyprus Application Deadline The deadline to apply is: Sunday, 20 September 2026 at 23:00 EEST Applicants should submit their applications before the stated deadline. The organisers aim to notify successful applicants by 23 September 2026 . Selected participants will then receive a detailed programme for the workshop. How to Apply Eligible applicants should complete the official online application form before the deadline. Application Form: Apply for Youth Connect: Youth Champions for Environment and Peace Participation in the programme is free . For further information or enquiries, applicants can contact: UNFICYP: unficyp-youthchampions@un.org Application Tips Before submitting your application, applicants should: Confirm your age and location: Make sure you are aged 18–30 and currently living in Cyprus. Check the workshop dates: Participation on 3, 4, 10 and 11 October is mandatory. Demonstrate genuine motivation: Explain your interest in environmental issues, peacebuilding, and a sustainable future for Cyprus. Highlight relevant interests: Previous environmental activism is not required, but applicants should demonstrate an interest in environmental and peacebuilding issues. Show your willingness to collaborate: The programme specifically involves working with participants from different communities. Check your access requirements: Make sure you have the documentation needed to enter the UN buffer zone in Nicosia. Apply before the deadline: Submit your application by 20 September 2026 at 23:00 EEST. Conclusion The Youth Connect: Youth Champions for Environment and Peace 2026 programme offers young people living in Cyprus an opportunity to combine environmental action with peacebuilding and intercommunal cooperation . Through an immersive four-day workshop, participants will learn from experts and activists, develop relationships across communities, form teams, and create environmental action plans. Selected teams will then receive small grants and mentorship to implement their initiatives by February 2027. The programme is open to young people aged 18–30 from all communities living in Cyprus, and previous experience in environmental peacebuilding is not required. Interested applicants should ensure they can commit to all four workshop days and meet the programme s access requirements before applying. Application deadline: 20 September 2026 at 23:00 EEST. title: Longview Philanthropy COO / Director of Operations 2026 | Apply by 6 September
summary: Longview Philanthropy is inviting applications for a senior Chief Operating Officer (COO) or Director of Operations position to help the organisation rapidly scale its team, systems, and operations. The opportunity is designed for an experienced operations leader who has successfully managed organisational growth and can build effective teams, processes, and functions in a fast-paced environment. Longview says candidates do not necessarily need previous experience in AI safety or philanthropy and expects strong applicants may come from rapidly scaling startups and technology companies. About Longview Philanthropy Longview Philanthropy advises major donors and makes grants in areas including AI safety and nuclear weapons policy . Its mission is to help the world navigate extreme risk and unlock an excellent future. The organisation states that it directed more than $75 million to high-impact organisations in 2025 and expects its activities to grow substantially in 2026. Longview currently has offices in Berkeley, New York City, Washington DC, and London . As Longview plans significant growth in 2027 and beyond, it is seeking a senior operations leader who can help the organisation scale while maintaining its effectiveness, agility, and high standards. About the COO / Director of Operations Role The successful candidate will be appointed as either: Chief Operating Officer (COO), or Director of Operations The final title and scope will depend on the candidate s experience. The role reports to Longview s current COO, Katie Hearsum, as she transitions into another senior position, or to CEO Simran Dhaliwal. The organisation is looking for someone who can operate at a senior leadership level, manage multiple operational functions, and build systems capable of supporting rapid organisational growth. Key Responsibilities Help Longview Double in Size One of the central responsibilities is helping Longview significantly expand its workforce and organisational capacity. The successful candidate will: Design and execute an operations and hiring strategy to support the organisation s growth. Work with the Office of the CEO and leadership team to determine which functions need to be developed and when. Own the operations organisational structure and hiring decisions. Scope roles and help close strong candidates. Maintain a high standard for excellence and organisational fit. Build strong relationships between operations and other departments. Ensure that regulatory requirements are appropriately managed across the US and UK entities. Develop Operations Leaders The COO or Director of Operations will manage and develop leaders responsible for several critical functions. These currently include: People Operations Business Operations Finance Talent Grants Management The successful candidate will coach these leaders and help them navigate the challenges associated with a rapidly scaling organisation. The role will also involve setting the standard for how operations functions across Longview, including promoting clear ownership, direct feedback, high-quality decision-making, and a mission-focused approach. Build New Operational Functions Longview is looking for a leader capable of expanding the scope of traditional operations functions. For example, the successful candidate may be responsible for developing a finance function that handles both internal financial activities and investment of capital held by the organisation. The role may also involve creating a recruiting function that not only supports Longview s own hiring needs but also helps identify founders for new organisations that Longview s grantmakers want to support. Build Systems and Processes for Growth Another major responsibility will be developing systems that allow Longview to grow without unnecessarily creating bureaucracy. The successful candidate will: Build simple and robust systems for planning and decision-making. Determine when additional structure is useful and when it may become counterproductive. Streamline routine operational activities. Standardise processes where appropriate. Automate operational work, including through AI. Provide operational support that allows grantmakers and advisors to focus on specialised work. Longview also states that it is open to tailoring the role for exceptional candidates and may consider a different scope or title where appropriate. Ideal Candidate Longview is looking for an experienced operations leader who has successfully guided organisations through rapid growth. The ideal candidate is expected to be: An experienced manager of managers. Comfortable working across multiple operational functions. Experienced in fast-paced environments. Highly capable of prioritising competing demands. Confident working through organisational ambiguity. Interested in coaching and developing people. Essential Experience Candidates should ideally have experience in the following areas: Experience Scaling Organisations Applicants should have scaled operations at a fast-growing organisation, preferably at the 30-to-60-person stage or beyond , and understand the challenges and failure modes that can occur during organisational growth. Managing Geographically Distributed Teams Candidates should be comfortable managing teams and working effectively across different locations. Managing Managers Experience managing managers during periods of significant organisational growth is an important requirement. Multiple Operational Functions Candidates should have been responsible for at least three operational functions . Longview s current operational functions include People Operations, Business Operations, Finance, Talent, and Grants Management. Critical Abilities The successful candidate should demonstrate strong judgement and operational leadership. Longview particularly values candidates who: Know when processes create value and when they create unnecessary bureaucracy. Can move quickly and prioritise effectively under pressure. Are comfortable managing multiple competing priorities and changing deadlines. Enjoy coaching and developing people. Can tackle new problems without relying on an established playbook. Are comfortable operating in ambiguous environments. Communication and Collaboration Skills Strong communication will be important in the role. Candidates should be: Exceptionally clear written and verbal communicators. Comfortable adapting to Longview s working style. Able to prepare effective agendas and support memo-based decision-making. Confident pushing back on colleagues when necessary, regardless of seniority. Comfortable giving and receiving direct feedback. Proactive in providing candid feedback. Motivation and Organisational Fit Longview wants candidates who are genuinely motivated by its mission. Previous knowledge of AI safety or philanthropy is not required , but candidates should care about the problems Longview works on and understand how the organisation s mission influences its decision-making. The organisation is also looking for people who are: Kind and conscientious. Energised by fast-paced, lean working environments. Comfortable taking ownership. Committed to professional excellence. Additional Experience That Would Be an Advantage The following experience is considered useful but is not required : Hands-on experience with grants management. Non-profit compliance experience. Experience working in regulated-industry operations. Previous exposure to AI safety. Previous experience in philanthropy. Longview explicitly encourages strong candidates to apply even if they do not meet every qualification listed in the vacancy. Salary and Compensation The advertised total compensation depends on the position offered: Director of Operations: $165,000–$264,000+ Chief Operating Officer: $220,000–$330,000+ These figures include base salary and a 10% unconditional pension/401(k) contribution . Benefits Longview provides a range of benefits, with specific benefits depending on the employee s location. Benefits for US Staff US employees may receive: 100% employer-paid private health insurance through UHC. Dental and vision coverage. 25 vacation days, plus public holidays and additional winter-break days. Four months of fully paid family leave. $3,000 annual professional development budget. Well-being support of up to $200 per month for gym memberships and fitness classes. In-office meals and a stocked office fridge at most US offices. Benefits for UK Staff UK employees may receive: Private health insurance through Aviva. 25 days of holiday plus bank holidays and additional winter-break days. Four months of fully paid family leave. £5,000 annual well-being budget. £2,400 annual professional development budget. Equipment and support for establishing a productive work environment. In-office meals and a stocked office fridge. Benefits are subject to eligibility requirements and applicable waiting periods. Location Longview prefers candidates who can work in person at one of its offices in: Berkeley, United States Washington DC, United States New York, United States London, United Kingdom The organisation states that it is able to sponsor visas in the United States and United Kingdom . Start Date The successful candidate is expected to start as soon as possible , with the exact start date to be agreed between Longview and the successful applicant. Application Process Longview plans to use a thorough but relatively fast recruitment process. The process is expected to include: An application form. A paid strategy work task. Interviews with leadership and direct reports. Reference checks. A paid two-day in-person work trial. Longview states that the process may be tailored for individual candidates. How to Apply Interested candidates should complete the official Longview Philanthropy application form. Apply here: Longview Philanthropy COO / Director of Operations Application Candidates should ensure their application clearly demonstrates relevant experience in organisational scaling, operations leadership, management, hiring, systems development, and cross-functional collaboration. Application Deadline The application deadline is: Sunday, 6 September 2026 — End of Day Applications are being reviewed on a rolling basis , so interested candidates are encouraged to apply as early as possible. Important Information for Applicants This is a senior-level operations leadership position , rather than an entry-level or graduate opportunity. Candidates should therefore carefully assess their experience against Longview s expectations, particularly experience managing managers, overseeing multiple operational functions, and scaling organisations. However, Longview states that most strong candidates will not have every qualification listed and encourages candidates who are uncertain about meeting every requirement to apply. About Longview s Work Longview Philanthropy was founded in 2018 to advise major donors on reducing extreme risks. The organisation has four departments: Operations Donor Advising AI Grantmaking Nuclear Grantmaking Longview describes its team as collaborative and dedicated, with a culture centred on clear communication, professional development, direct feedback, ownership, excellence, and outcomes. Conclusion The Longview Philanthropy COO / Director of Operations opportunity is aimed at experienced operations professionals who can help a growing organisation scale its people, systems, processes, and functions while maintaining a high standard of effectiveness. The successful candidate will play a central role in organisational growth, including managing operational leaders, expanding teams, developing new functions, improving systems, and supporting strategic decision-making. With compensation of up to $330,000+ for the COO position , additional benefits, and opportunities to work across Longview s offices in the United States or United Kingdom, the role represents a significant senior leadership opportunity for an experienced operations professional. Candidates who have successfully scaled organisations and are motivated by Longview s mission should consider applying before the 6 September 2026 deadline . title: RCOY Africa 2026 Delegates Call for Applications | Regional Conference of Youth in Accra, Ghana
summary: The Regional Conference of Youth (RCOY) Africa 2026 is inviting young Africans to apply for delegate participation in the upcoming regional youth climate conference, taking place in Accra, Ghana, from 18–21 October 2026 . RCOY Africa brings together young climate leaders, researchers, innovators, entrepreneurs, policymakers, civil society representatives, Indigenous Peoples, and development partners to strengthen youth participation in Africa s climate agenda. The 2026 conference will provide a platform for young people across Africa to exchange ideas, develop regional solutions, strengthen their technical knowledge, and contribute to youth priorities ahead of COP31 . About RCOY Africa 2026 The Regional Conference of Youth (RCOY) is the regional edition of the Conference of Youth (COY) , held ahead of the annual United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Conference of the Parties. RCOY Africa serves as a major platform for African youth engagement in the global climate process. The conference builds on the outcomes and recommendations generated through Local Conferences of Youth (LCOYs) organised across African countries. These national youth perspectives are brought together at the regional level to help develop a unified African youth position. The outcomes of RCOY Africa 2026 are intended to contribute to the global youth agenda and inform youth engagement at COP31 . RCOY Africa 2026 Theme The theme of the 2026 conference is: Driving Integrated Solutions Across Africa s Climate Agenda for Impact, Resilience and Justice. The theme reflects the need for coordinated and inclusive approaches to addressing Africa s climate challenges while promoting resilience, justice, and meaningful impact. Who Should Apply? The RCOY Africa 2026 delegate application is open to young people who meet the basic eligibility requirements and can demonstrate meaningful engagement with climate-related issues. Applicants must: Be between 18 and 35 years old at the time of the conference. Be a citizen or resident of an African country . Demonstrate an interest or engagement in climate-related issues. Be able to contribute meaningfully to conference discussions and activities. The selection process is competitive because the number of fully and partially funded places is limited . Selection Criteria Applications will be assessed based on several factors, including: Motivation Applicants should demonstrate a clear motivation for participating in RCOY Africa 2026 and explain why the conference is relevant to their work, interests, experience, or aspirations. Leadership Demonstrated leadership experience will be considered as part of the selection process. This may include leadership in climate initiatives, youth organisations, community projects, research, advocacy, entrepreneurship, or other relevant activities. Climate Engagement Applicants should demonstrate meaningful involvement or interest in climate action and related areas. This could include work or engagement in areas such as climate policy, climate justice, environmental sustainability, adaptation, mitigation, renewable energy, biodiversity, youth advocacy, or community resilience. Diversity and Inclusion The selection process will also consider diversity and inclusion to ensure broad representation among participating delegates. Regional Representation Applicants from different African countries and regions will be considered to support broad regional representation at the conference. Potential Contribution Applicants will also be assessed based on their potential to contribute meaningfully to discussions, activities, knowledge exchange, and the wider objectives of RCOY Africa 2026. Funding and Participation Participation is competitive, and fully and partially funded delegate opportunities are limited . The information provided for the call does not specify that every selected participant will receive full funding. Applicants should therefore carefully review the application information and any communication from the organisers regarding the specific funding arrangement attached to their selection. Conference Location and Dates Event: Regional Conference of Youth (RCOY) Africa 2026 Location: Accra, Ghana Dates: 18–21 October 2026 Age Range: 18–35 years Eligible Region: African countries Important Application Requirement Applicants are specifically required to complete the application in their own words . The organisers state that the use of generative AI to write application responses is not permitted . Applicants should therefore ensure that all personal statements, motivation responses, and other written answers submitted through the application form accurately reflect their own experiences, perspectives, and ideas. Using AI-generated responses could conflict with the organisers application requirements. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the RCOY Africa 2026 Delegates Call is: Wednesday, 9 September 2026 at 11:59 PM GMT Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours. How to Apply Interested applicants should complete the official online application form and provide the information requested by the organisers. Application Form: Apply for RCOY Africa 2026 Applicants should carefully read each question and provide accurate information based on their own experiences. For questions or enquiries about the application, applicants can contact: Email: rcoyafrica2026@gmail.com Why RCOY Africa 2026 Matters RCOY Africa provides an important platform for young Africans to participate in conversations surrounding the continent s climate future. Africa faces significant climate-related challenges, including vulnerability to extreme weather events, food and water insecurity, climate-induced displacement, ecosystem degradation, and challenges associated with sustainable development. Young people have an important role to play in developing and advocating for solutions to these challenges. Through RCOY Africa, participants can engage with other young leaders and stakeholders, exchange knowledge, strengthen regional collaboration, and contribute African youth perspectives to the broader international climate process. Connection to COP31 One of the important functions of RCOY Africa is to help consolidate youth perspectives ahead of the annual UN climate negotiations. The 2026 regional conference will build on recommendations from Local Conferences of Youth across Africa and help bring together national perspectives into a broader African youth position. This provides participants with an opportunity to contribute to discussions that can inform youth engagement in the international climate process leading towards COP31 . What Kind of Applicants Should Consider Applying? The call may be particularly relevant to young Africans involved in or interested in: Climate change Climate policy Climate justice Environmental sustainability Renewable energy Climate adaptation Climate mitigation Sustainable development Environmental advocacy Youth leadership Research and innovation Green entrepreneurship Community development Resilience building International climate negotiations Applicants do not necessarily need to come from one specific academic discipline. What is particularly important is their demonstrated interest, engagement, leadership, motivation, and potential contribution to the conference. Application Tips Before submitting your application, consider the following: Check your eligibility: Confirm that you are 18–35 years old and a citizen or resident of an African country. Use your own words: The organisers explicitly prohibit the use of generative AI to write application responses. Be authentic: Your responses should accurately describe your experiences, climate engagement, leadership journey, and motivation. Demonstrate impact: Where appropriate, explain what you have done rather than simply stating that you are interested in climate action. Explain your motivation: Clearly communicate why participating in RCOY Africa 2026 matters to you. Submit early: Do not wait until the final hours before the deadline to complete the application. Review before submitting: Check that all required sections have been completed and that your information is accurate. Conclusion The RCOY Africa 2026 Delegates Call for Applications offers young Africans an opportunity to participate in a major regional youth climate platform in Accra, Ghana, from 18–21 October 2026 . With a focus on impact, resilience, justice, regional collaboration, and integrated climate solutions , the conference will bring together young people and other stakeholders working to advance Africa s climate priorities. Eligible young Africans between 18 and 35 years old who are citizens or residents of African countries are encouraged to consider applying. Because funded spaces are limited and the selection process is competitive, applicants should prepare their applications carefully and submit them before the 9 September 2026 deadline . Most importantly, applicants should remember that the organisers require application responses to be written in the applicant s own words and do not permit generative AI to write those responses.
